svg.title: 2006–2024 series (RCID v1), regimes & NNA gaps
svg.desc: Three-panel infographic under the RCID v1 rule. Panel A displays the 19 estimable annual cohorts for progression failure or grade lag from 2006 to 2024: all 19 point estimates are positive, ranging from 0.94 to 28.22 percentage points, with a median of 7.18 and an exposed-weighted aggregate of 9.11 points whose Manski bounds span 0.43 to 16.21. Panel B shows attenuation across institutional regimes from 12.15 points in 2006–2010 and 7.82 in 2011–2015 to 5.29 in 2016–2019, 2.70 in 2020–2022, and 2.59 in 2023–2024. Panel C shows G minus 1 baseline gaps after exact matching: individual SEP eligibility is balanced at minus 1.07 points, whereas exposed students face lower school SEP agreements at minus 10.06 points, lower full-day schooling at minus 18.54 points, lower valid record coverage at minus 19.24 points, and higher prior school switching at plus 16.52 points.
